title: Tension chords
status: First draft, written before you started Level 1. Before printing, re-tune it from your Level 3 check-in sheet and practice log: pairs, targets and tempos are best guesses.
summary: Chords whose job is to pull somewhere: dominant 7ths and their 9, 13 and 7♯9 cousins, the diminished 7th that repeats every three frets, half-diminished and augmented — and the chromatic lines (line clichés, walking slash chords) that make plain progressions sound arranged. Something is built on a descending line cliché and a C → C7 → F secondary dominant; Say Yes walks one finger down string 4 under a held G.
goals: Play a dim7 shape at all four of its positions, and use it as a passing chord between chords a whole step apart.
Play 9, 13, m7♭5 and 7♯9 voicings, and say what each adds to the plain chord.
Something with the record: line cliché, intro tag and the bridge in A.
Say Yes with the record (tuned down a whole step), the bass walk clean.
Name the secondary dominants and line clichés in a song you are learning.

reading.note: week 2 — secondary dominants and line clichés.

song_plan: Core: **Something** (Song day weeks 1–2) and **Say Yes** (weeks 3–4); Session D plays both. Say Yes is recorded a whole step low: tune down (D G C F A D) to play along — shapes as charted. Swap a core song for an alternate when you can already play it with the record, or when its hard change is still under 15 a minute after two weeks. Alternates, easiest first: *Karma Police* (G → F♯ barre), *Some of Them Are Old* (augmented, 6 and 7 colours over F), *Michelle* (dim7, m6, a minor line cliché — the hardest song in the program so far).

week_plan.fretboard: The tritone: 3rd and ♭7 of E7, A7, D7, G7 on strings 4 and 3

week_plan.fretboard: Secondary dominants in C: A7 → Dm, E7 → Am, D7 → G

exit_criteria: Benchmarks 1–6 at target in two Session Ds in a row.
Something with the record, no stops (refrain line cliché and bridge included).
Say Yes with the record, tuned down, no stops.
Named a root, play its dim7 at two different frets within five seconds (five roots).
Say the job of each chord in Something's refrain and of C7 in the verse, without looking it up.
stuck: Not every box ticked after 6 weeks? Move on anyway. Keep one song from this level (a core song or an easier alternate) as a 5-minute play-through in Level 5's Session D, and open every Level 5 Session A primer with your weakest pair until it reaches target.
skip_ahead: Pass every benchmark cold (first attempt, no practice that day) in week 1's Session D? Go straight to Level 5.

drills.title: One-minute changes
drills.instructions: Timer at 1:00. One down-strum per chord, change, strum the other, as fast as you can while staying clean. Count clean landings only. Two rounds per pair; write the better count.

drills.title: Air shapes
drills.instructions: Hand off the neck. Form the whole shape an inch above the strings, land all fingers at once, strum, check every string, lift. Ten per shape.

drills.title: Place and lift
drills.instructions: Fret the shape, relax until the fingers just touch, press again. Twenty presses, one per click at 60, no strumming.

drills.title: Anchor hunt
drills.instructions: Before a new pair, say what stays (anchor), what slides along its string (guide) and what jumps. Then ten changes keeping anchors down. This level: C → Cmaj7 → C7 = only one finger moves each time; Am → Am(maj7)/G♯ → Am/G → D9/F♯ = the Am fingers stay, only the bass moves; G/F → G/E → G/D = little finger stays on string 1 fret 3; dim7 = the whole shape slides 3 frets.

drills.title: Change loop
drills.instructions: Strum chord 1 once, change, strum chord 2 once, stop, reset. Ten clean in a row; a miss sets the count back to zero.

drills.title: Tempo ladder
drills.instructions: One chord per bar, four down-strums (or the song's figure). Start where it is perfect (try 50). Three clean passes: +4 bpm. A miss: −8 bpm. Write the top clean tempo in today's blank.

drills.title: Eyes closed
drills.instructions: Make the change without looking; open your eyes after landing to check. Ten times.

drills.title: Song loop
drills.instructions: Loop the two bars around the hard change in the song's own rhythm, 10 bpm under this week's tempo. Then add a bar either side. Then the whole section.

drills.title: Random pairs
drills.instructions: Write the 15 chord names from the chord page on scraps. Draw two, do one-minute changes, write the pair and count on the back of the sheet. Draw again.

drills.title: Diminished every three frets
drills.instructions: Fdim7 xx3434: play it at frets 3, 6, 9 and 12 (the whole shape up three frets each time) — the same four notes, re-stacked. One per beat at 60. Then as a passing chord, two beats each: **C** x32010 → **C♯°7** xx2323 → **Dm** xx0231 → **G7** 320001, and **G** → **G♯°7** xx0101 → **Am7** x02010 → **D7** xx0212.

drills.title: Line cliché
drills.instructions: One per bar at 60, then two beats each. **Minor:** Am x02210 → Am(maj7)/G♯ 4x2210 → Am/G 3x2210 → D9/F♯ 2x2210 (Something's refrain). **Major:** C x32010 → Cmaj7 x32000 → C7 x32310 → F 133211 (Something's verse). Sing the moving note.

drills.title: Dominant colours
drills.instructions: Over an open low E: E7 020100 → E9 020102 → E13 020120 → E7♯9 x7678x (let the open E ring). Two bars each; say what each adds: 9 (F♯), 13 (C♯), ♯9 (G — the minor 3rd over a major chord).

drills.title: The Say Yes walk
drills.instructions: Little finger on string 1 fret 3 all the time. G 3x0003 → G/F♯ 2x0003 → … bridge: G → G/D♯ xx1003 → G/E xx2003 → G/F xx3003 → G/E → G/D xx0003. One finger walks string 4; pick the bass, then strum. One per beat at 60.

drills.title: Find the tritone
drills.instructions: In a dominant 7th the 3rd and ♭7 are a tritone apart. E7: G♯ (3rd) on string 4 fret 6 + D (♭7) on string 3 fret 7. Find the same pair for A7, D7 and G7. Resolve each: 3rd up a half step, ♭7 down a half step — E7's pair becomes A and C♯, notes of A.

drills.title: Connect the boxes
drills.instructions: A minor pentatonic box 1 (frets 5–8) up, slide on string 3 into box 2 (frets 7–10), down box 2, back into box 1. Eighths. Then add the blues note (E♭: string 5 fret 6, string 3 fret 8).

drills.title: Make something
drills.instructions: Key of C or Am. Four chords including one tension move: a dim7 passing chord, a secondary dominant (A7 before Dm, E7 before Am) or a line cliché. Loop; each pass change one thing. Write the keeper in Notes.

benchmarks.name: 1 · C → C♯°7 → Dm → G7, two beats each, bpm

sessions.name: A
sessions.title: Chord day
sessions.focus: New shapes and this week's three pairs (week plan, column 1). Pair 1 is the hard one.

blocks.title: Primer: today's shapes
blocks.instructions: Dim7 slide at 60 (frets 3-6-9-12, 1 min). Then air shapes ×10 on both chords of pair 1. Carried a weak pair from Level 3? Change-loop it for the last minute.

blocks.title: Pair 1: the full recipe
blocks.instructions: Anchor hunt (say what stays, slides, jumps) → slow motion ×5 → change loop to 10 clean → tempo ladder from 50, one chord per bar. A chain of chords? Ladder the whole chain. Stop at the clock.

blocks.title: Pairs 2 and 3
blocks.instructions: Change loop to 10 clean on each, then one-minute changes: two rounds each. Write the better count.

blocks.title: Line clichés
blocks.instructions: The minor (Am …) and major (C …) lines from the drill page, one per bar, then two beats each. Hum the moving note.

blocks.title: Fretboard: dominant colours
blocks.instructions: E7 → E9 → E13 → E7♯9 over the open low E, two bars each. Name the added note each time.

blocks.title: Song: put pair 1 back in
blocks.instructions: In this week's song section: song loop on the two bars with pair 1, then the section ×2 at this week's tempo.

blocks.title: Log
blocks.instructions: Log page: tick A, write the minutes. In Notes: the change that felt worst today.

sessions.name: B
sessions.title: Fretboard day
sessions.focus: Where tension lives on the neck: the blues note, the tritone, connected boxes, secondary dominants (week plan, column 2).

blocks.title: Primer
blocks.instructions: Air shapes ×10 on the two chords of pair 1, then the change with eyes closed ×10.

blocks.title: Find the tritone
blocks.instructions: 3rd and ♭7 of E7, A7, D7 and G7 on strings 4 and 3, each resolved by half steps into its I chord.

blocks.title: This week's scale
blocks.instructions: Week 1 box 1 (+ blues note), week 2 box 2, weeks 3–4 box 1 → box 2 connected. Say the root at every square. Quarters at 60, then eighths on the tempo ladder.

blocks.title: Passing and secondary chords
blocks.instructions: Dim7 as a passing chord (C → C♯°7 → Dm → G7; G → G♯°7 → Am7 → D7), two beats each. Then in C: C – A7 – Dm – G7 and C – E7 – Am – D7 – G7, saying which chord each 7th points at.

blocks.title: Song by numbers: Something
blocks.instructions: Verse in C: I, Imaj7, I7 (= V7 of IV), IV, II (D), V. Refrain: vi with the line cliché, then ♭VII (E♭). Play verse and refrain ×2 at this week's tempo, then the verse in G by numbers: G Gmaj7 G7 C A D.

blocks.title: Log
blocks.instructions: Log page: tick B, write the minutes. Notes: what on the fretboard is still slow.

sessions.name: C
sessions.title: Song day
sessions.focus: Longest song block: isolate this week's hard change (pair 1), then play the section and the song in time. Weeks 1–2 Something, weeks 3–4 Say Yes (tune down a whole step to play with the record).

blocks.title: Primer
blocks.instructions: Place-and-lift ×20 and air shapes ×10 on the two chords of pair 1.

blocks.title: The hard change
blocks.instructions: Change loop to 10 clean, then tempo ladder one chord per bar from 50.

blocks.title: Fretboard: name the jobs
blocks.instructions: Read this week's section. Above each chord write its number and, for any chord outside the key, its job: secondary dominant, borrowed, passing, line cliché.

blocks.title: This week's song
blocks.instructions: Song loop round the hard change (5 min). The week's section ×3 at this week's tempo. Then the whole form without stopping — fumble through. Weeks 3–4: the last 5 minutes with the record.

blocks.title: The other core song
blocks.instructions: Once through at this week's tempo for it. Mark any bar that broke and give it one song loop.

blocks.title: Log
blocks.instructions: Log page: tick C, write the minutes. Notes: the bar where you stopped, if any.

sessions.name: D
sessions.title: Mix and measure
sessions.focus: Short versions of everything, the benchmarks with numbers, one review from Level 3, and five minutes of your own music.

blocks.title: Primer
blocks.instructions: Air shapes ×5 on every chord in benchmarks 3–5. The tests are taken cold.

blocks.title: Benchmarks
blocks.instructions: One-minute changes, one round each: **3** C7 ↔ F · **4** E♭ ↔ G · **5** G/F ↔ G/E. Tempo ladder from 60 for **1** C → C♯°7 → Dm → G7, **2** the Am line cliché and **6** box 1 → box 2 in eighths. Write all six numbers in the log.

blocks.title: Review from Level 3
blocks.instructions: Triad climb in G (strings 1-2-3) and nearest inversion G – Em – C – D, then one-minute changes G/D 7-8-7 ↔ C/E 9-8-8 — or the pair you carried from Level 3.

blocks.title: Songs, measured
blocks.instructions: Something, then Say Yes (tuned down) — with the record from week 3, at this week's tempo before that. Write benchmarks 7 and 8 in the log.

blocks.title: Make something
blocks.instructions: C or Am: four chords with one tension move (dim7 passing chord, secondary dominant or line cliché). Loop, change one thing per pass, write the keeper in Notes.

blocks.title: Log and exit check
blocks.instructions: Tick D in the log. Tick any exit box you passed today. Week 6 or all boxes ticked? Fill in the check-in sheet.
